clue.text: Following inquest, use lab experimentally

indicators.note: working experimentally means trying things in new orders, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: After an inquest, the lab is put to use in trials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'experimentally' shuffles the thirteen letters of INQUEST, USE and LAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something coming later in sequence, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Outwardly cunning, work on Greek character with sentimentality

indicators.note: outwardly says the cunning word sits on the outside, wrapping what follows

parts.note: cunning means sly
OP is short for opus, a work
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A wily person mawkishly tackles a Greek figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outwardly' says the cunning word wraps around the work and the Greek letter; 'on' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb of manner: doing something in a soft, mawkish way means with sentimentality.

clue.text: Conservative to support campaign with Germany — can monarch?

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a war is a military campaign
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
can is slang for a toilet, as is loo
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A Tory wonders whether a king can back a war alongside Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is not the verb but slang for a toilet, LOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservative outlook favours the past over change, i.e. it is nostalgic and reactionary.

clue.text: Prefer to have head slightly down for dash

indicators.note: in a down clue the first letter moving slightly down means it drops one place

parts.note: to lean towards something is to prefer it

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to bow their head a little for a quick exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have head slightly down' moves the L of LEAN down one place, giving ELAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash as in flair and verve is a synonym for this borrowed French word for style.

clue.text: New first lady wearing French article is odd

indicators.note: the French article is worn around the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A new First Lady sporting a French item looks peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' means the French article is worn around the rest. 'First lady' suggests a president's wife; here it is the Bible's first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd number cannot be evenly divided, so the phrase 'is odd' describes something not even.

clue.text: Tick seen creeping around clothing

indicators.note: creeping around suggests the letters are wandering into a new order

explanation.surface: A tick has been spotted crawling over someone's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creeping around' rearranges TICK SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ties worn at the neck are items of clothing, an example for a general class.

clue.text: Shrewd partners due to leave summit after one

indicators.note: after places the rest of the wordplay following the letter for one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
N and S are partners at bridge, North and South

indicators.note: the summit of a word is its top letter, which must leave

parts.note: what is due to you is rightful

explanation.surface: Climbing partners are expected to come down from the summit after one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave summit' drops the R from RIGHTFUL; 'after' puts I first.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrewd person shows perceptive understanding, a near synonym.

clue.text: 'Drink, drink' chanted goon with such swaggering

parts.note: a cat laps up a drink
chanted means sang

indicators.note: swaggering suggests the words strutting about out of place, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A swaggering goon chants a demand for drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swaggering' rearranges GOON and SUCH into SOUCHONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoky black China tea is a drink, an example of the category.

clue.text: Waters around river rising north spread

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, so backwards
the watering word goes around the river letter

parts.note: waters means wets

explanation.surface: Floodwaters spread north as a river rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts R inside WETS to make WERTS, which 'rising' turns into STREW.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewn means scattered or spread about, a past participle synonym.

clue.text: Best to let go of tool

parts.note: the pick of the bunch is the best
to axe someone is to let them go from a job

explanation.surface: Someone advises that it is best to release a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy digging implement is a tool, an example of the category.

clue.text: In retrospect, civic amenity site's flash place for waste

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a civic amenity site is a council rubbish dump, known in Britain as a tip
a flash is an instant, a sec

explanation.surface: Looking back, the council dump turns out to be a showy spot for rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: A civic amenity site is the British official name for a public rubbish dump. 'In retrospect' reads both pieces backwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit where sewage collects is literally a place for waste.

clue.text: State radio was not totally needed

indicators.note: not all the letters of the phrase are needed, so the answer lies inside it

explanation.surface: A national broadcaster was found to be partly surplus to requirements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not totally needed' finds the answer inside 'radIO WAs'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Midwestern member of the American union is a state, an example of the category.

clue.text: Religious texts on church I mark as 'C'

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
NT is the New Testament
a grade is a mark given for work

explanation.surface: A cleric grades scripture and church papers with a C.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the scriptures follow the church.
explanation.definitionFit: C is the standard abbreviation for the Celsius temperature scale.

clue.text: Stand accompanying bongo, saving good Parisian's energy

parts.note: to stand is to get up
and joins one thing to accompany another

indicators.note: saving here means except, so those letters are left out

parts.note: bon is French for good

explanation.surface: A bongo player stands up while sparing a Parisian's energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' means except: BONGO without BON leaves GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Get-up-and-go is an idiom for drive and vigour.

clue.text: Name European in court that's told stories

indicators.note: the name and European letters go in the court

parts.note: a courtyard, or yard, is a court

explanation.surface: A European named in court is the one who told tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N and E inside YARD.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin a yarn is to tell a tale, so the verb means narrated stories.

clue.text: Exercising: one path to get in good shape

indicators.note: the good letter has to get in among the shuffled ones
exercising suggests the letters being worked out and moved about

explanation.surface: Exercise on a path is a way to get into good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercising' rearranges ONE PATH and 'to get in' puts G among them.
explanation.definitionFit: A seven-sided polygon is a geometric figure, an example of a shape.

clue.text: Pull up outside university and worry one protecting property

indicators.note: the pulled word goes outside the university letter
in a down clue up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to drag is to pull
to dog is to worry or hound someone

explanation.surface: Someone parks outside a university fretting about its security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DRAG into GARD, and 'outside' wraps it round U to make GUARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch animal kept to keep intruders off premises protects property.

clue.text: Computing system you might find on chopper

definitions.meaning: a branch of maths that is a system for calculating
a chopper is slang for a tooth, and the word also means tartar deposited on teeth

explanation.surface: A computer system might be found aboard a helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopper' suggests a helicopter or axe; here it is a tooth, and the word is also the dental name for tartar.
explanation.definitionFit: Differential and integral maths is a computing method; in dentistry the word names hardened plaque.

clue.text: Not posh in suit, instead I'm revealing shins

indicators.note: not says the posh letter is taken away from the suit
instead says another piece is put in its place

parts.note: clubs is one of the four card suits
U means upper-class, posh
taken as written, IM

explanation.surface: Not dressed up in a suit, someone shows off bare shins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' and 'instead' swap the U of CLUBS for IM.
explanation.definitionFit: To shin up a tree is to clamber up it, so shins is a verb meaning scales.

clue.text: Dynastic members, son and daughter involved in defeat must return

indicators.note: the daughter letter is involved in, placed within, the defeat word
returning means the word for defeat is read backwards

parts.note: a rout is a heavy defeat

explanation.surface: Members of a ruling family, children included, must come back after a rout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must return' turns ROUT into TUOR; 'involved in' puts D inside it, and S is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The English royal house of Henry VII and Elizabeth I were members of a dynasty.

clue.text: Third of sackings in one month concerning staff

indicators.note: the picked letter goes in the month

parts.note: Sept is short for September

indicators.note: the third letter of the word sackings is taken

parts.note: re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: A third of staff were sacked in one month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third of' takes C from sackings; 'in' puts it inside SEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial rod carried by a monarch is a kind of staff.

clue.text: Book's precis should have length cut, the French murmur

indicators.note: cut says the length letter is removed

parts.note: a blurb is the summary on a book's cover
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An editor demands the book summary be shortened, with French murmurs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops L from BLURB to leave BURB.
explanation.definitionFit: To babble or mumble softly is a synonym for this verb.

clue.text: Adoring tour, do sail around

indicators.note: around suggests the letters being moved about into another order

explanation.surface: A fan invites someone on a tour to go sailing around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges TOUR, DO and SAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Worshipping something as an idol means devoted or doting.

clue.text: Pine store's not opened

indicators.note: not opened says the start of the word is missing

parts.note: a cache is a hidden store

explanation.surface: A store of pine wood remains unopened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not opened' drops the first letter of CACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine for something is to long or yearn for it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Perhaps elder said to be superior to old for some performers

indicators.note: in a down clue, superior means placed above
said means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: elder is an example of a tree

explanation.surface: An elder is described as superior to old performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps elder' suggests an older person; it is the tree. 'said' gives TRI, and 'superior to' puts it above O.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of three musicians is some performers.

clue.text: Cursed pupils not working

definitions.meaning: effing and blinding is swearing, so this past tense means swore
eyes whose pupils do not work have lost sight

explanation.surface: Schoolchildren who are idle get sworn at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupils' looks like schoolchildren; it is the eye. The British phrase 'effing and blinding' means swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing sight means the eye's pupils fail; in British slang the verb also means swore.

clue.text: Call for tiresome person to be expelled is justified

parts.note: a bore is a tiresome person
out is the call to send someone away

explanation.surface: Demanding that a dull person be thrown out is fair.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a call, the pieces shout to send the bore away.
explanation.definitionFit: When facts bear out a claim they support it, so the past tense means confirmed or vindicated.

clue.text: Prince admitting one groupie heartlessly hit kisser

indicators.note: the prince admits the letter for one inside his name

parts.note: George is a royal prince's name
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: hit suggests the letters knocked into a new order
heartless means the centre letter of groupie is taken out

explanation.surface: A prince lets a groupie in, then cruelly strikes the one who kissed him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' drops the U from GROUPIE, and 'hit' rearranges GROPIE into PORGIE.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme this boy kissed the girls and made them cry, so he is a kisser.
